headline: BTC holds $83.4K but the hl-cycles invalidation level is now 1.8% away (ETF cost basis $81.7K, was 2.5%), as Brent rebounds to about $106 into September CPI today and ETH OI sits at z30 -1.8
tldr: Regime: hl-cycles mild risk-on (66% BTC, 4 days; 2 of 6 stress conditions on, up from 1). Main change: Fear & Greed rebounded 57 to 62 while HL OI stayed flat at $11.7B, so no leverage is returning; hl-cycles momentum fell to +18 from +61 a week ago, and no series is at |z30| >= 2 (closest: ETH OI -1.8, BTC DVOL +1.7). Main disagreement: equities at highs (S&P 7,805, VIX 15.3) and risk-on regime sit against a Restrictive Macro lens (33), a 5.24% 10Y and Brent near $106. Next catalysts: Sep CPI (Oct 14 per most outlets; one says Oct 15), Russia/Iran sanctions item Oct 18 (unverified this run), FOMC Oct 27-28. Not financial advice.

domains.summary: Yields were little changed at the latest print: 10Y 5.24% and 2Y 4.80% on Oct 9 (FRED; Oct 12 bond holiday, Oct 13 not yet posted), 30Y 5.60%, and the 2s10s was +42bp on Oct 13 (+44bp Oct 9), a mild flattening driven by the front end rising (2Y +5bp) rather than the long end. The broad dollar index was 121.60 on Oct 9 (+0.6% from 120.90 on Oct 6). FRED Brent stops at $125.44 on Oct 6, but live reports put Brent near $106-107 on Oct 13-14 (Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia cited), so oil is lower than the FRED print yet still above $100, which keeps an inflation input alive; the two sources are a week apart, so we treat the level as low-confidence. Effective fed funds is 3.88%. Futures price roughly a 19-20% chance of an October hike. September CPI consensus is about 3.6-3.7% headline (0.5% m/m) and 2.5% core (0.2% m/m); outlets disagree on whether it prints today or Oct 15. We read policy as restrictive. A headline print above 3.7% would likely raise October hike odds; a print at or below 3.6% with oil easing would likely keep the hold priced. hl-cycles Macro lens: 33 (Restrictive).

The US cash close of Oct 13 (FRED): S&P 500 7,805.45 (flat), Nasdaq Comp 27,204.38 (-0.15%), Dow 51,670.10 (-0.35%). Over 5 sessions SPY is -0.1%, QQQ -2.1% and IWM -1.6% (Yahoo), so the index is flat while growth and small caps lag. VIX 15.27 (+0.4% on the day, 5d +1.7%), still calm. Futures were slightly higher early Oct 14 ahead of CPI and the start of Q3 earnings. The read is a quiet index masking weakness in semis (SMH -7.0% over 5 sessions) against platforms; calm VIX against a 5.2% 10Y is the part we would not rely on. A VIX close above 18 would suggest the CPI print is being taken as a shock. No put/call ratio found.

Price/OI/funding: BTC -0.3% 24h ($83,403 HL mark) with OI $3.15B (z30 -0.7, from $3.21B) and funding +0.0008%/h (z30 +0.8) is mild deleveraging, with neither side pressing. ETH is the weak spot: -1.1% with OI $2.70B at z30 -1.8, the lowest reading in the set, so ETH longs are leaving even though ETH funding is positive (z30 +0.8). SOL -1.2% and HYPE -1.9% with OI flat. HL total OI is $11.7B (z30 -1.1, mean30 $12.0B), unchanged on the day. Fear & Greed rebounded 5 points to 62 (z30 0.0, at its 30-day mean), so the Oct 13 washout in sentiment has been retraced without OI rebuilding: a bounce on thin participation. Crowding is low: funding skew z30 +0.8, no asset above +0.9. BTC DVOL 38.2 (z30 +1.7) is the nearest series to the |z| 2 line, i.e. options buyers are paying up while perp leverage is flat, which fits a market hedging into CPI. BTC dominance 59.2% (z30 -0.1). Stablecoin supply $313.1B (z30 +0.5, flat). BTC (-0.3%) held while Nasdaq futures and Korean stocks fell on Oct 13 (CoinDesk), so crypto looks idiosyncratic rather than macro-driven (low-confidence; the 5d QQQ -2.1% vs BTC flat agrees). What would change the read: OI back above $12.0B with funding z30 above +2 would mean leverage is returning.

Oct 13 closes (Yahoo), with 5-session change: META $762.50 (+2.6% day, +3.2% 5d), MSFT $543.45 (+0.4%, +2.7%), AAPL $341.27 (+0.1%, +2.3%), GOOGL $353.78 (+0.3%, +1.8%), AMZN $258.58 (-0.4%, +0.9%), NVDA $228.52 (+1.0%, -4.5%). SMH $588.12 fell 0.5% on the day and is -7.0% over 5 sessions. Dispersion persists: platform and software names hold gains while the semis complex, led by NVDA (about 22% of SMH), is the weak spot; NVDA's one-day bounce did not move SMH. SMH closing back above $600 would suggest the semis stress is fading; a further 5% fall from $588 would suggest it is spreading. Q3 earnings begin this week; dates for the six names were not verified this run.

Searches this run returned no dated reporting on the Oct 18 Russia/Iran sanctions implementation date flagged last run, so that item is carried from late-September reporting (the Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, signed Sep 18, with tariffs of up to 100% on top buyers of Russian energy and a broad national-interest waiver) and is unverified this week. What we can cite for Oct 13-14: Middle East supply worries, including reported Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, have Brent near $106-107. Linkage: an actual tariff on a top oil importer would plausibly add to the inflation input ahead of the Oct 27-28 FOMC; a waiver or delay would likely remove that risk. Brent closing above $110 would suggest the supply shock is widening.

thesis.observe: BTC $83,403 (HL mark, -0.3% 24h); HL OI $11.7B (z30 -1.1), flat on the day; ETH OI $2.70B (z30 -1.8); Fear & Greed 62 (from 57); BTC funding +0.0008%/h (z30 +0.8); BTC DVOL 38.2 (z30 +1.7); no series at |z30| >= 2. hl-cycles: mild risk-on 4 days, 2 of 6 stress conditions on (STH-SOPR below 1, ETF 7d outflow -11.7K), momentum +18 (from +61 a week ago), Compass 48 (Neutral), Macro 33 (Restrictive); ETF cost basis $81.7K (1.8% below), True Market Mean $79.3K (4.9% below), STH cost basis $74.3K. S&P 7,805 (Oct 13), VIX 15.3, 10Y 5.24% (Oct 9), Brent about $106 (live reports Oct 13-14).
thesis.infer: Positioning: price flat, OI flat to lower, funding barely positive means neither longs nor shorts are pressing; ETH is where leverage is leaving. Sentiment bounced (F&G 57 to 62) without OI, and DVOL at z30 +1.7 shows hedging demand into CPI, so the bounce looks thinly supported. Disagreement: equities at highs and a risk-on hl-cycles regime sit against a Restrictive macro lens, a 5.2% 10Y and oil above $100, while hl-cycles momentum has faded from +61 to +18 and stress conditions rose from 1 to 2. Consensus is pricing a low chance of an October hike; we read September CPI and the December path as the test.
thesis.forecast: Base case (we lean here, low-confidence): BTC chops between the ETF cost basis ($81.7K) and the mid-$80Ks with OI subdued through CPI, confirmed by daily closes above $81.7K and HL OI staying below $12.0B. Tail case (low-confidence): a hot CPI (headline above 3.7%) or an oil spike sends a daily close below $81.7K, which hl-cycles lists as invalidating its read, and risk skews to a test of the True Market Mean ($79.3K, about 4.9% below). Second tail case (low-confidence): a soft CPI revives leverage, with HL OI back above $12.0B and BTC funding z30 above +2 turning a rally fragile. Consensus is pricing a hold in October; we read the risk as sitting in the December path.
thesis.disclaimer: Not financial advice. Market intelligence only — a reasoned read of public data, not a recommendation to buy or sell anything.

risks: Daily BTC close below $81.7K (ETF cost basis, hl-cycles invalidation level; 1.8% below spot)
HL total OI above $12.0B (30d mean) with BTC funding z30 above +2 (leverage returning, fragile rally)
SMH closing below $559 (a further 5% fall from $588; semis stress spreading to the index)
